subject: anatomy
title: Aortic Arches and Embryonic Venous Systems

steps.tx: During the fourth and fifth weeks, six pairs of aortic arch arteries sprout from the aortic sac, coursing through the pharyngeal arches to connect with bilateral dorsal aortae. The **first aortic arch** largely regresses, leaving only a small portion that forms the maxillary artery, which supplies the deep facial structures and maxillary teeth.
steps.say: In weeks four and five, six pairs of aortic arch arteries connect the aortic sac to the dorsal aortae through the pharyngeal arches. The first arch artery regresses, contributing only to the maxillary artery supplying the jaws.

vis.alt: Aortic arches and vascular wall architecture
vis.caption: Embryonic aortic arch distribution and vessel development. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The second aortic arch likewise atrophies, leaving remnants that form the embryonic stapedial artery and the hyoid artery. The **third aortic arch** develops into the common carotid artery and the proximal segment of the internal carotid artery, while the distal internal carotid derives from the cranial continuation of the dorsal aorta.
steps.say: The second aortic arch atrophies, contributing only the stapedial and hyoid arteries. The third aortic arch forms the common carotid artery and the base of the internal carotid, while the cranial dorsal aorta completes the cerebral vessel.

steps.tx: The fourth aortic arch exhibits marked asymmetrical evolution between left and right sides. On the left, the **fourth aortic arch** forms the segment of the definitive aortic arch between the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries. On the right, it forms the proximal portion of the right subclavian artery.
steps.say: The fourth arch develops asymmetrically: on the left, it builds the central span of the definitive aortic arch between the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries. On the right, it forms the proximal right subclavian artery.

steps.tx: The fifth aortic arch is entirely transient, either failing to form or degenerating rapidly without leaving adult derivatives. The **sixth aortic arch**, or pulmonary arch, gives off branches to the developing lung buds. On the left side, its distal portion persists throughout fetal life as the muscular ductus arteriosus, shunting deoxygenated blood away from collapsed fetal lungs.
steps.say: The fifth arch regresses completely. The sixth arch sends branches to the lung buds. On the left, its distal portion forms the ductus arteriosus, shunting pulmonary blood away from nonventilated fetal lungs directly into the descending aorta.

steps.tx: The embryonic venous drainage is mediated by three paired venous systems entering the sinus venosus. The **vitelline veins** drain the yolk sac, traversing the septum transversum. Hepatic cords growing into the septum break these veins into hepatic sinusoids. The vitelline network gives origin to the portal vein, superior mesenteric vein, and the terminal segment of the inferior vena cava.
steps.say: Three paired venous systems empty into the sinus venosus. Vitelline veins drain the yolk sac and pass through the liver, forming hepatic sinusoids. They give rise to the portal vein, superior mesenteric vein, and the terminal inferior vena cava.

steps.tx: The **umbilical veins** carry oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the chorionic villi of the placenta to the sinus venosus. The right umbilical vein obliterates early in week six. The left umbilical vein persists throughout gestation, establishing a bypass channel called the ductus venosus through the liver to channel oxygenated blood directly into the inferior vena cava.
steps.say: The umbilical veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the heart. The right umbilical vein regresses early, leaving the left umbilical vein as the sole conduit. Inside the liver, it forms the ductus venosus to direct blood into the inferior vena cava.

steps.tx: Somatic embryonic drainage depends upon the **cardinal veins**, comprising anterior cardinal veins draining the head and posterior cardinal veins draining the torso. These unite to form short common cardinal veins (ducts of Cuvier) entering the sinus horn. An anastomosis between anterior cardinals develops into the left brachiocephalic vein, while the right anterior cardinal forms the superior vena cava.
steps.say: Somatic drainage relies on paired cardinal veins: anterior cardinals drain the head and posterior cardinals drain the torso. An oblique anastomosis between anterior cardinals forms the left brachiocephalic vein, while the right anterior cardinal becomes the superior vena cava.

rows: Renal segment of inferior vena cava

steps.tx: Complex anastomoses between subcardinal and supracardinal veins assemble the definitive **inferior vena cava**, built from four distinct developmental segments: the hepatic segment (vitelline), prerenal segment (subcardinal), renal segment (subcardinal-supracardinal anastomosis), and postrenal segment (supracardinal). Failure of these venous anastomoses produces duplicated or left-sided inferior vena cava.
steps.say: The inferior vena cava forms from four developmental pieces: hepatic, prerenal, renal, and postrenal segments derived from vitelline, subcardinal, and supracardinal veins. Incomplete fusion leads to duplicated or left-sided inferior vena cava anomalies.
